text:
maria: Quick prototype dump — made a SKU-affinity heatmap to show which routes/models are sticky to specific SKUs. Wanted feedback before I wire it into the cost dashboard.
jay: Nice. Are you correlating by routing policy or by actual backend allocation (i.e., which GPU pool served the request)?
maria: Right now it's by final routing decision + model SKU served. So it shows SKU X is used 72% of requests for route /summarize, and that route mostly hits dedicated-pool-3.
kevin: Important: cache savings get attributed to the route, not SKU. If you show both at the same granularity it confuses billing. We had tickets where teams thought cache saved SKU cost rather than route savings.
sam: +1 to making a clear separation. Maybe split columns: "requests served by SKU" vs "amortized token cost after cache credits". Also add sampling note — our telemetry is 1:10 for hot routes right now.
maria: Good call. UX idea: heatmap cells = color by raw token-cost; border thickness = cached-savings %. Hover shows breakdown: raw tokens, cache credits, effective token cost, route-affinity %. Thoughts?
jay: Hover breakdown is perfect. But be explicit about sampling bias. Add a small badge: "sampled 10%" and link to docs. Also include timeframe selector (last 24h / 7d / 30d) — affinity changes fast during rollouts.
kevin: Implementation note: to compute amortized token cost we need to join two streams: token-metering + cache-credit ledger. That join is heavy. Consider pre-aggregating per-invocation key in goroutine batcher and emitting daily aggregates to the warehouse.
maria: Agreed. Proto SQL I'm using for the warehouse join:
```
SELECT sku, route, sum(tokens) as tokens, sum(cache_credit_tokens) as cache_credits
FROM invocation_agg
WHERE ts >= '2026-03-10' AND sampled = true
GROUP BY sku, route;
```
This is just proto, we can refine.
sam: One more UX ask: include an "affinity delta" toggle to compare two windows (canary vs baseline). Ops needs to catch if new routing policy suddenly pins traffic to a higher-cost SKU.
kevin: For that we'll need to surface confidence intervals — with sampling 10% the variance can be large for low-volume routes. Suggest throwing out cells with <100 sampled invocations unless explicitly requested.
maria: Makes sense. I'll add the threshold and a tooltip explaining it.
costbot: deploy-check: no heavy join queries on main-prod cluster between 09:00-18:00 PST. Schedule backfill job for 02:00 UTC.
maria: Thanks @costbot. I'll schedule the daily pre-agg job and post a follow-up with mock screenshots.
jay: If you want, I can prototype the hover breakdown component in Storybook — would help get product buy-in quickly.
maria: Please do. Tagging UX in a follow-up. Thanks all! :thumbsup:
